title: Icing takes a little patience: Bakery Shop Icing / Decorator's Icing / Strawberries à la Creme
attribution: Corryine De Souza, Herald writer (Recipe Swap, Calgary Herald); Bakery Shop Icing from Betty Gladu; Decorator's Icing from Linda Homenick; Strawberries à la Creme from Chris Mulders
ingredients: === Third recipe: Strawberries à la Creme ===
8 cups strawberries, hulled, washed and thoroughly dried
directions: — Bakery Shop Icing —

Cream butter, shortening, sugar and vanilla together in a large bowl. Stir cornstarch into milk and add to sugar mixture. Beat everything at low speed until all ingredients are blended. Beat at medium speed for 5 to 7 minutes until the icing is creamy smooth and of desired consistency.
Note: This icing will appear curdled at first but don't give up. As you continue to beat it, it becomes smooth.
=== Second recipe: Decorator's Icing ===
Beat egg whites until stiff, set aside. Cream shortening, add 1/2 cup powdered sugar; cream 2 minutes. Add beaten egg whites, flavoring and remaining sugar. Cream again.
=== Third recipe: Strawberries à la Creme ===

Cut strawberries in half and sprinkle with the confectioners sugar, toss and chill for about 15 minutes. Using an electric mixer, whip the cream till stiff peaks hold their shape. Toss the Kirsch/brandy into the berries and gently fold in the whipped cream. To add the final touches, refrigerate 8 serving glasses and then dip the rims into sugar, place mixture into glasses and refrigerate at least one hour. Place a whole strawberry on the top and serve.
notes: Newspaper clipping, RECIPE SWAP column, Calgary Herald
Thanks to Betty Gladu for sending this recipe as requested by Laura MacIntosh
Linda Homenick has had this recipe for over 35 years and still uses it faithfully. This icing gives good detail. It gets crispy on the outside and stays soft inside.
Strawberries à la Creme compliments of Chris Mulders

raw_text:
RECIPE SWAP
Icing takes a little patience
CORRYINE DE SOUZA, Herald writer
Thanks to Betty Gladu for sending this recipe as requested by Laura MacIntosh:
Bakery Shop Icing
1/2 cup butter
6 tablespoons shortening
1 cup white sugar
2 teaspoons vanilla
1 tablespoon cornstarch
1/2 cup warm milk
Cream butter, shortening, sugar and vanilla together in a large bowl. Stir cornstarch into milk and add to sugar mixture. Beat everything at low speed until all ingredients are blended. Beat at medium speed for 5 to 7 minutes until the icing is creamy smooth and of desired consistency.
Note: This icing will appear curdled at first but don't give up. As you continue to beat it, it becomes smooth.
Here's another recipe for Laura McIntosh. Linda Homenick has had this recipe for over 35 years and still uses it faithfully. This icing gives good detail. It gets crispy on the outside and stays soft inside.
Decorator's Icing
3/4 cup of shortening
3 cups powdered sugar
2 egg whites
1/2 teaspoon flavoring
Beat eggs white until stiff, set aside. Cream shortening, add 1/2 cup powdered sugar; cream 2 minutes. Add beaten egg whites, flavoring and remaining sugar. Cream again.
This recipe is compliments of Chris Mulders. He shares this simple and elegant desert with our readers.
Strawberries à la Creme
8 cups strawberries, hulled, washed and thoroughly dried.
1-1/4 cups confectioner's sugar
1 pint heavy cream
1/2 cup Kirsch or Brandy
Cut strawberries in half and sprinkle with the confectioners sugar, toss and chill for about 15 minutes. Using an electric mixer, whip the cream till stiff peaks hold their shape. Toss the Kirsch/brandy into the berries and gently fold in the whipped cream. To add the final touches, refrigerate 8 serving glasses and then dip the rims into sugar, place mixture into glasses and refrigerate at least one hour. Place a whole strawberry on the top and serve.
Thanks to the many readers who responded to Kitty Mah's request for Amish Bread. Unfortunately, I have not recieved a starter recipe and I need it before I print the bread recipe.
■ Joyce Davis has lost her buckwheat pancake recipe. The recipe used only buckwheat-no wheat flour. It called for yeast and had to be made the night before.
■ Jacqueline Dunlop is looking for a seafood aspic mould.
■ Ken Saunders would love to find a recipe for salmon spread. It is usually served as an appetizer with crackers.
